scope: One transferable prerequisite-recovery mechanism; three new target instances and three pre-existing queue fixtures. No L_P, numerical-core change or comparative-effectiveness claim.
decision_rule: Choose the feasible listed action with the smallest declared intervention credit, then alphabetical ID. Credits order options in this experiment; measured execution and representation effort are reported separately.
holdout_policy: Both fixed selectors and the case protocol are frozen before target executions. A digest of all target-instance predictions is calculated and locally persisted before any target intervention runs; this is not external preregistration. Opaque case IDs are not selector inputs. Action IDs identify outputs and break exact cost ties, but are not used as diagnostic clues. Missing/stale receipt families were explored during discovery: these are held-out executions, not previously unseen problem families, blinded human reasoning, or independent test-set generalization.

mapping.source: Required payload identity w2 must be completed, in addition to w1 and w3.
mapping.target: A receipt with passed=true and the exact current input_fingerprints must exist at verification_checks.json before package.py can pass its receipt gate.
mapping.preserved: Exact job identities; exact file names, byte counts and SHA-256 values. Jobs are not mapped to abstract throughput totals.

mapping.source: w2 is in backup_payload_ids but absent from pending_fifo_payload_ids and completed_payload_ids.
mapping.target: A real prior verification receipt is retained outside the active observatory folder while its required active path is missing.
mapping.preserved: The target backup is an experimental handoff condition, not a claim that package.py implements a backup service. It is copied byte-for-byte from an actual successful verification.

mapping.source: Replay appends available missing backups before tick 1, preserving payload identities.
mapping.target: Copy the retained receipt into the required path; do not change its passed field or fingerprints.
mapping.preserved: Receipt content is source evidence; no verdict flag is inserted into the method's case facts.

mapping.source: An absent required identity cannot be replaced by a different job or created by a higher service rate.
mapping.target: A correctly named file with the wrong input snapshot cannot substitute for current verification; a stale assembled HTML also defeats a full re-verification attempt.
mapping.preserved: Availability, revision identity and independent completion constraints are separate predicates.

mapping.source: Queue rate is measured in jobs/tick and interacts with a three-tick deadline.
mapping.target: The package code has no service-rate setting. Three concurrent calls test repeated processing without prerequisite repair, not a quantitative queue-throughput law.
mapping.preserved: No conversion between queue time, call concurrency, execution seconds and credits is introduced.

falsifier: The strongest direct falsifier is a case whose exact current compatible receipt is available, all independently specified package constraints hold, and byte-identical restoration nevertheless fails to produce a valid current archive. A prediction mismatch is reported, never relabeled as a success. Stale receipts and stale assembly are explicit boundaries, not that strongest falsifier.

analogy_levels.descriptive_resemblance: Both tasks can look stalled while repeated processing is available. That appearance alone does not justify an intervention.
analogy_levels.shared_structure: A named required prerequisite is absent from the active set; an identity-compatible retained token can enter the active set without altering its content, subject to other constraints.
analogy_levels.intervention_transfer: Transfer is supported only where the actual target executable accepts the restored compatible receipt and produces a verified archive. Replaying a stale receipt and re-verifying stale assembly must be rejected.

limitations: This is a fixed-rule mechanism pilot. The role representation performs inspectable typed constraint propagation, but neither method is an open-ended reasoner and this is not a CANON superiority benchmark.
The target is pre-existing software acceptance code from the same local project, frozen before this pilot, not an independent external operational dataset.

The receipt gate trusts passed and exact input fingerprints; it does not authenticate receipt origin or independently rerun every test. The experiment uses genuine generated receipts, but cannot generalize acceptance to a cryptographic verification guarantee.
Case families were selected after code inspection. Target instance execution is held out from selector execution; the family design is not blind and the sample is too small for efficacy estimates.

The alternate verification action assumes the same executable, test and data inputs as the actually checked seed, with only a documented README change allowed. Arbitrary revisions and runtime/environment failures require a richer model.
No build repair is offered in the stale-assembly case. Rejection means none of the three listed actions succeeds, not that the project cannot ever be repaired.
The original accepted evidence, standalone examples, numerical core, L_P reconciliation and data acquisition are untouched.
